title: Minimum Moves to Reach Target with Rotations
summary: In an n*n grid, a snake starting at positions (0, 0) and (0, 1) aims to reach the positions (n-1, n-2) and (n-1, n-1).
statement: In an n*n grid, a snake starting at positions (0, 0) and (0, 1) aims to reach the positions (n-1, n-2) and (n-1, n-1). The snake can move one cell to the right or down if the cell is not blocked. Additionally, the snake can rotate clockwise if it is in a horizontal position and the two cells directly below it are empty, or it can rotate counterclockwise if it is in a vertical position and the two cells to its right are empty. The goal is to determine the minimum number of moves required to reach the target positions, or return -1 if it is impossible.
constraints: The snake occupies two adjacent zero cells and begins horizontally at the top-left pair.
It may move right/down while horizontal, down/right while vertical, or rotate clockwise/counterclockwise through a clear two-by-two square.
Return minimum moves to finish horizontally in the bottom-right pair, or -1.
hints: Represent a state by the upper-left or leftmost cell plus orientation.
Breadth-first search legal translations and rotations, checking every newly occupied cell.
Deduplicate states and stop at the horizontal bottom-right state.
Every transition costs one, so BFS returns the minimum legal move count.
editorial: Every transition costs one, so BFS returns the minimum legal move count.

tests.explanation: A shortest legal sequence reaches the goal in eleven moves.
One downward move places the horizontal snake at the bottom goal.
